title: The uncle who cursed
hookLine: Abu Lahab curses him in front of all, and Surah al-Masad answers
tomorrow: The sun in my right hand

cards: Back at the foot of Safa. The clans have just said, we have only known you to tell the truth. He has just called himself a warner, before a severe punishment.
Some of them had left their work to come. Then a voice cuts across the crowd. Not a stranger's voice.
His own uncle's. Al-Bukhari keeps the words in Ibn Abbas's report: may you perish, was it for this that you gathered us? Today: Abu Lahab.

teach.b: He's known as Abu Lahab. That's a kunya, a 'father of' name, and tradition reads it as father of flame; the sources give his given name as Abd al-Uzza.
He was a son of Abd al-Muttalib, a brother of the Prophet's father, and he lived close by. Family. That is what makes the moment sting.

The report in al-Bukhari says that after his words, a surah came down: surah one hundred eleven, al-Masad, the palm fiber. Pickthall translates its first verse: "The power of Abu Lahab will perish, and he will perish."
The surah goes on to say his wealth will not help him, and it speaks of his wife carrying firewood, with a rope of palm fiber around her neck, which gives the surah its name.
The tradition reads it as Allah's answer, not as a nephew trading insults with his uncle. And look at what is missing from the scene.
On Safa, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is not reported to curse back. In the tradition's reading, the reply is the surah. A small hadith in al-Bukhari shows the same habit later.
Quraysh took to calling him Mudhammam, the blamed one, a twist on Muhammad, the praised one. He said to his companions: doesn't it amaze you how Allah turns their insults away from me?
They curse Mudhammam, and I am Muhammad.

teach.h: THE POWER OF ABU LAHAB WILL PERISH.
teach.b: The insult missed. A curse came at him in public, from family, and he didn't answer it with another.

how: Surah al-Masad (111) is a short surah that Muslims memorize and can recite in prayer; its occasion, Abu Lahab's words at Safa, is taught alongside it in tafsir and sirah study.

p: the uncle who cursed at Safa

s: Abu Lahab was a stranger to the family

the Prophet is reported to have cursed him back on Safa
the answer came in surah al-Masad, not in a reply of his own.

games.q: your own uncle curses you in front of the whole city. what do you do?
o: say nothing back, and leave the answer to Allah.
walk away and stop the message.
games.why: he is not reported to curse back; surah al-Masad came as the answer, and he kept going.

practice: Bring to mind one sharp word someone threw at you, maybe from family; you don't have to forgive it right now, or pretend it didn't hurt.
Just practice not throwing one back, even in your head: each time a reply rises, breathe out and let it drop. If you pray, you can leave the matter with Allah.

wordCard.voice: Abu Lahab. The uncle who answered the call from Safa with a curse, and the surah al-Masad that came down in reply. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a kunya, 'father of flame'; lahab means a flame.

carryVoice: Your line: let it go. An insult aimed at Mudhammam can miss its mark. See you tomorrow.
